nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a simple graph on a vertex set $V$ and let $A \subseteq V$. If $v$ is an external neighbour of $A$ in $G$, then $v$ is adjacent in $G$ to some vertex $a \in A$.

nodes.title: Independent sets in spectral expanders are small

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a simple graph on a finite vertex set $V$ with $n$ vertices, and let $C$ be a real number. Then $G$ is a $C$-expander if $C > 0$, every set $A \subseteq V$ with $|A| < n/(2C)$ has an external neighbourhood in $G$ with at least $C|A|$ vertices, and for any two disjoint sets $A, B \subseteq V$ with $|A| \ge n/(2C)$ and $|B| \ge n/(2C)$ some vertex of $A$ is adjacent in $G$ to some vertex of $B$.
nodes.title: C-expander

nodes.summary: The real square matrix `A` satisfies `‖A x‖ ≤ c ‖x‖` (Euclidean norms, written as `(A x) · (A x) ≤ c² (x · x)`) for every vector `x` whose entries sum to zero. For the adjacency matrix of a `d`-regular graph and `c = d λ` this is spectral expansion `λ(G) ≤ λ` in the sense of S. Vadhan, *Pseudorandomness* (2012), Section 4.1.2 and Definition 4.5.
nodes.title: Spectral bound on the vectors orthogonal to the constants

nodes.summary: For `N ≥ 2` vertices, the complete graph is a spectral expander of degree `N - 1` with parameter `λ = 1 / (N - 1)`: its adjacency matrix acts as `-1` on the vectors orthogonal to the constants, since `(A x)_i = ∑_{j ≠ i} x_j = -x_i` when `∑_j x_j = 0`. For it the lower bound `mul_sub_le_sq_mul_of_isSpectralExpander` is an equality.
nodes.title: The complete graph is a spectral expander

nodes.title: Spectral expander

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a simple graph on a finite vertex set $V$ and let $h$ be a real number. Then $G$ is a uniform vertex expander with parameter $h$ if $h > 0$ and every set $S \subseteq V$ with $|S| \le |V|/2$ has an external neighbourhood in $G$ with at least $h|S|$ vertices.
nodes.title: Uniform vertex expander

nodes.summary: If `G` is a `d`-regular spectral expander with parameter `λ`, then `xᵀ L x ≥ d (1 - λ) xᵀ x` for every `x` orthogonal to the constant vector, where `L = D - A` is Mathlib's Laplacian `SimpleGraph.lapMatrix`. Equivalently the second-smallest Laplacian eigenvalue is at least `d (1 - λ)` (the eigenvalue form is not formalized here). The proof: `xᵀ L x = d xᵀ x - xᵀ A x` and `xᵀ A x ≤ ‖x‖ ‖A x‖ ≤ d λ ‖x‖²`.
nodes.title: Laplacian Rayleigh quotient of a spectral expander

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a simple graph on a finite vertex set $V$ with $n$ vertices, let $C$ be a real number, and suppose $G$ is a $C$-expander. If $A, B \subseteq V$ are disjoint sets with $|A| \ge n/(2C)$ and $|B| \ge n/(2C)$, then some vertex $a \in A$ is adjacent in $G$ to some vertex $b \in B$.
nodes.title: Large disjoint sets in a C-expander span an edge

nodes.summary: Let `G` be a `d`-regular graph, `d ≥ 1`, on `N` vertices that is a spectral expander with parameter `λ`, and let `ℓ` satisfy `λ^ℓ N < 1`. Then any two vertices `s` and `t` are joined by a walk of length exactly `ℓ`; in particular `G` is connected with diameter at most `ℓ`, which is `O(log N / log (1 / λ))` for `λ < 1` (O. Reingold, *Undirected ST-connectivity in log-space*, ECCC TR04-094 (2004), Proposition 2.2,…
nodes.title: Spectral expanders have logarithmic diameter

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a simple graph on a vertex set $V$, let $A \subseteq V$ and let $v \in V$. Then $v$ lies in the external neighbourhood of $A$ in $G$ if and only if $v \notin A$ and $v$ is adjacent in $G$ to some vertex $a \in A$.
nodes.title: Membership in the external neighbourhood

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a simple graph on a finite vertex set $V$ and let $h$ be a real number. If $G$ is a uniform vertex expander with parameter $h$, then $h > 0$.
nodes.title: The parameter of a uniform vertex expander is positive

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a simple graph on a finite vertex set $V$ and let $C$ be a real number. If $G$ is a $C$-expander, then $C > 0$.
nodes.title: The parameter of a C-expander is positive

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a simple graph on a finite vertex set $V$ and let $h$ be a real number. If $G$ is a uniform vertex expander with parameter $h$ and $S \subseteq V$ satisfies $|S| \le |V|/2$, then the external neighbourhood of $S$ in $G$ has at least $h|S|$ vertices.
nodes.title: Small sets expand in a uniform vertex expander

nodes.summary: Let $C$ be a real number and let $G$ be a $C$-expander on a finite vertex set $V$. Then every set $A \subseteq V$ with $|A| < |V|/(2C)$ has at least $C|A|$ external neighbours, that is, at least $C|A|$ vertices outside $A$ are adjacent to some vertex of $A$.
nodes.title: Small sets expand in a $C$-expander

nodes.title: Spectral expanders have edge expansion, through Cheeger's inequality

nodes.summary: For a `d`-regular spectral expander with parameter `λ` on `N` vertices and every vertex set `S`, the number `e(S, V \ S)` of edges leaving `S` satisfies `d (1 - λ) |S| |V \ S| ≤ N e(S, V \ S)`. This is the expander mixing lemma with `T = V \ S` (S. Vadhan, *Pseudorandomness* (2012), remark after Lemma 4.15: Part 1 of Theorem 4.14 follows by setting `T = Sᶜ`).

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.
